findings.issue: The option withdraws the documented default handoff through an undocumented header; it does not remove the call. Explain the lost/reinterpreted default rather than claiming the call is removed.
The option adds an unknown response value. It does not require a new input; explain that older clients reject the new enum value.
The option replaces a response value with an object. It does not require a new request input; diagnose the breaking response shape.
The option adds a new response state, not a request input; v1 clients treat unknown states as terminal errors.
The option changes InvoiceId meaning on reissue. Explain loss of stable obligation identity, not a required input.
The option redefines “revoked” to include pending; it does not remove a call. Explain changed state meaning and old-client incompatibility.
The option sends a new state through an existing field, not a new input. Explain that old readers reject the value.
The option replaces accepted/rejected response status with reason text. It does not require a request input.
The option removes stable IDs from the current catalog, not the call; explain broken progress references.
The option changes default response contents and asks old clients to filter; explain the changed active-only contract, not a new input.
